title: Calvyn Justus’s First Phygital Piece: Splashing Swim Legacy into Fashion
content:
## _Calvyn Justus, a former Olympic swimmer turned digital fashion designer, shares his journey and the inspiration behind the JUSTUS x FVCKRENDER collection, featuring_[ _the unique FVYN// Pants_](https://www.instagram.com/p/C-8C3atPOMp/) _._

* * *

> **_Can you introduce yourself and share a bit about your background?_**

Originally from South Africa, I began competing as a swimmer at the age of 9, joining my first national senior team at 17 and my first Olympics at 20. This journey allowed me to travel extensively and work with various brands as a model and ambassador. After the Olympics, I moved to Los Angeles at 23, where I started collaborating more with high fashion and beauty brands.

Now, as a digital artist with a passion for fashion, I've built my career through diverse creative roles in the industry. During the pandemic lockdown, I taught myself 3D tools, immersing myself in technology to express my ideas for the future of fashion. My work has earned recognition in prestigious galleries around the world, including New York, Tokyo, and London, and has been featured in prominent publications such as i-D, Numéro, and GQ.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1c3c544fd7f249fdac2610d06a630214/images/bf1ff1c4d3b7496a92ca1ba58e9778c3combined%20image.png)

  
**_How has your background as a swimmer and model contributed to your digital creations?_**

This is where I started my introduction to the fashion world, eventually working behind the camera as well, producing and directing commercials and other creative projects. Today, my unique life experiences shape my perspective; my sporting background influences my creative work, providing me with the space I need from the sporting world so I can balance training and performance without feeling overwhelmed.

 

> **_What led you to explore 3D design, and how did you find CLO?_**

As I began teaching myself 3D, I came across CLO, which helped me see fashion and garment design in a completely different light. It felt easy to use and not as overwhelming as most traditional fashion academic systems make one feel. That gave me the confidence to keep exploring and experimenting. I quickly saw the benefits of being able to design digitally and how many issues it fixed and gaps it bridged. Now, any ideas or concepts I have, I can design and manipulate them in CLO, perfecting the garment before moving on to physical production—saving several rounds of sample design iteration.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1c3c544fd7f249fdac2610d06a630214/images/4de8dc1f7f8d4007b491d5939a280e93JUSTUSxFVCKRENDERPress1-ezgif.com-resize%20%281%29.jpg)

> **_Can you describe the design process of your garment in CLO?_**

With regard to the selected artwork, the entire design and concept process was done in CLO, where I was experimenting with different shapes and panels, looking for ways to incorporate various materials. Leaning into my swimming past for reference, I landed on the neoprene and denim combo, with winged/shark fin-shaped panels—another reference to my past as a swimmer. The CLO program provided the playground for me to test the garment shapes and how they fall, move, and look—an integral part of producing the garment.

On top of that, the potential within the CLO program to showcase and present your designs in creative ways is incredible and limited only by your imagination. For my Neoprene and Denim pant design, I could experiment with different weights and fabrics before production, allowing me to explore all avenues the design could take and land on the best variation.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1c3c544fd7f249fdac2610d06a630214/images/441fc2b9370241c58ef69c19bb7de2e3JUSTUSxFVCKRENDERPress3-NoLogo-ezgif.com-resize.png)

> **_What is your favorite feature of CLO, and how does it help you as a designer?_**

For me personally, my favorite CLO feature has to be how simple it is to manipulate the garment. For example, adding wind or gravity (or removing gravity) and seeing how the garment interacts with the updated environment can allow for new ideas and innovative ways to present the design. Seeing how it moves and responds within the program simulation also gives the designer a lot of valuable feedback for potential corrections before producing.

 

> **_What advice would you give to aspiring digital fashion designers who want to follow in your footsteps?_**

My advice is literally to just start! CLO is so beginner-friendly, and there are so many [educational resources online](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D4Y1p1n69c0&list=PLqL8Ymi3Z68CT5n7Oz5CGXTFkIwClOmbi) about digital design and CLO that you really can start with no prior knowledge. I'm still learning every day; I just have the option to produce while I'm learning, which, in my mind, increases the speed of learning and adapting to mistakes as you're seeing them in real-time in the program, as opposed to waiting two weeks for a sample to arrive and then correcting. You can start anywhere, anytime, and I’m pretty sure there’s a free trial too—so there are no excuses, hahaha! Bring your ideas to life!

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1c3c544fd7f249fdac2610d06a630214/images/4c3c011c21cb4926876a4143ae696ed7IMG_7813.jpg)
content_description: Explore Calvyn Justus's inspiring journey from Olympic swimmer to digital fashion designer, and discover the creative process behind the innovative JUSTUS x FVCKRENDER collection, featuring the unique FVYN// Pants.

title: How Taskin Goec uses CLO as a Mixed Reality Designer
content:
Explore the story of Taskin Goec, a Mixed Reality Designer based in Berlin, who utilizes CLO in his entirely hybrid fashion design process.

In this video, he will share his workflow, demonstrating how he moves from experimentation to producing high-fidelity visuals. His digital-first approach allows him to enhance his creativity, adaptability, and efficiency.

"I find that working with CLO is much more dynamic. It allows me to be experimental and quick and try out tons of different things up until the production level. Because designing clothes for production can be quite costly, and with CLO, I make this process much more streamlined." – Taskin Goec

Find out more about Taskin's work here: [https://www.instagram.com/taskingoec/](https://www.instagram.com/taskingoec/)

title: The Future is 3D: How Lindex uses CLO for Fashion Design & Patternmaking
content:
Come with us behind the scenes of the Swedish fashion brand Lindex, and learn how they use CLO to shorten lead times in design & development and reduce their reliance on physical samples. CLO is especially key for prints and patternmaking in the kids' department at Lindex.

"I like to experiment with different technical solutions when I create my patterns. CLO enables me to do this without wasting any resources, and I can see the results of my patterns straight away. I can now make sure that the fit and size is exactly like my designer has envisioned before I send out any final patterns."

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/bb8d554c10c54a298dd639cb8e988560/images/7acbe32686f54814a1cfc3b15e70d0e0maxresdefault.jpg)
content_description: Explore how Lindex leverages CLO technology to revolutionize their design and development processes, enhancing efficiency and creativity in their kids' fashion line.

title: From Dream to Dress: The making of a fairy dress by Vesna
content:
## _Discover the enchanting world of Vesna as she shares her journey into digital fashion and the creation of the stunning dress from her_[ _Fairy-Tale series_](https://www.instagram.com/p/C4alkJIAI4o/) _using CLO._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6a195be291d84440981743b001b89a51/images/e5b392184b38485782cdeab44ca820d6Orchidea3D_FairyDress.png)

> **_Can you introduce yourself and share a bit about your background?_**

My name is Vesna Stawa, a 3D designer from Belgrade, Serbia. With a master's degree in photography, my expertise lies in lighting and texturing and later extends to hard surface modeling. My love for fashion and art direction has always fueled my creative pursuits. Being inclined towards digital creation, this pursuit naturally led me to the world of digital fashion and CLO.

 

> **_What inspires your work, and where do you typically find your creative influences?_**

Drawing inspiration from the Slavic goddess of spring, my name Vesna embodies my love for eternal spring, flowers, and fairies. Exploring avenues to convey my vision through clothing has always been a dream of mine.

 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6a195be291d84440981743b001b89a51/images/855108cad93e468081f6d9050bc7896ccombied%20image%20resized.png)

> **_Can you describe the concept behind your Fairy-Tale series?_**

This dress marks the beginning of my Fairy-Tale series of digital dresses. I imagined a magical garden where fairies might dance under the soft glow of light, and one of the dresses the fairies wear is this one.

The bodice is fitted and shimmering in a pale, soft pink, with a slight cinching at the waist, giving it a corseted appearance. The skirt is full and layered with pink floral patterns on a semi-sheer fabric that cascades down in voluminous ruffles. Underneath, there are additional layers of fabric in a slightly lighter, almost silvery shade, adding texture and depth.

> **_What was your design process for this dress in CLO?_**

I started with some reference images and then experimented in CLO. The real magic in digital production happens when you play around with different fabric blends, volumes, proportions, and colors. The digital creation process in CLO feels like exploring the magical fairy tales I imagine.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6a195be291d84440981743b001b89a51/images/23b25b7de7044075b4135e3913a13e33Capture2.JPG)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6a195be291d84440981743b001b89a51/images/7d5b376775cb4187862ed299355b463aCapture3.JPG)

> **_Can you share a specific challenge you faced during the design process and how you overcame it?_**

One of the biggest challenges is maintaining confidence in the final result. While I enjoy the speed with which I can visualize my ideas in 3D, that speed can also present a challenge. The tricky part is choosing one idea to focus on and committing to refining it, which often involves a slow, repetitive process. Staying patient through this phase is essential, especially when aiming for realistic results in designs with complex volumes and high polygon counts.

For instance, when I was working on my Fairy Dress, creating the voluminous skirt posed a unique challenge. The initial low-poly version (particle distance 20 and above) didn't capture the desired texture and movement; it looked too rigid. However, when I switched to a high-poly version (particle distance 5), the dress came to life, with the volume flowing in a more natural and captivating way. That transition required patience and trust in the final result.

One technique that helps me is breaking the design into different stages. After completing each stage, I take a short break before revisiting the work with fresh eyes. This process of stepping back allows me to see the bigger picture and make adjustments that improve the overall design. I recommend this approach to other CLO users as well—sometimes, a simple break can make all the difference in gaining a fresh perspective after focusing on details for too long. It helps you find a balance between the minutiae and the overall vision.

 

> **_Do you have any tips for other CLO users looking to enhance their designs, particularly in creating textures or experimenting with fabrics?_**

Experimentation is key to expanding your attention to detail—after all, you can only create what you’re able to perceive. Take the time to play around with different textures and observe how they transform the overall look and feel of a design. It’s a valuable way to train your eye to notice subtle variations. And, most importantly, always finish the projects you start, even the experimental ones. Revisiting a completed piece later can give you a fresh perspective, helping you better understand your initial approach and ideas. It’s often easier to see the potential and progress in a fully realized concept rather than just fragmented parts.

In CLO, [experimenting with textures](https://www.instagram.com/p/C-IQgcXq6P4/) is particularly accessible, thanks to tools like the [AI Texture Generator](https://www.instagram.com/p/C5QpFVFAzk7/). This feature allows you to create and modify textures quickly, making it an intuitive way to push the boundaries of fabric manipulation. Don’t be afraid to explore and let the digital medium guide your creative journey.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6a195be291d84440981743b001b89a51/images/7d5422dd85394fef8ec21757b07cc686Capture5.JPG)

> **_How does the digital creation process in CLO enhance your creativity?_**

It is very easy to get immersed in the world of digital creation, as you don't have to think about physical fabrics and the waste that physical experimenting generates. You have the full focus on the idea, and you can create anything that you can imagine.

 

> **_What are your future projects, and how do you see your work evolving in the digital fashion landscape?_**

Currently, my focus is on digital clothing and animation, but I’m eager to delve deeper into designing accessories like bags. I also aim to integrate my manual illustrations and artwork into my digital fashion creations, blending traditional and digital techniques. In the coming months, I plan to experiment with different ways to achieve this fusion, adding a more personal touch to my digital pieces.

I’m always open to new creative challenges, and if I come across unexpected discoveries during this journey, I’ll be excited to share them. For me, the evolution of my work is about exploring new horizons while staying true to the ethereal, fairy core aesthetic that defines my style.
content_description: Explore Vesna's enchanting journey into digital fashion as she unveils the captivating design process behind her stunning Fairy-Tale dress created using CLO.

title: DENIMVERSE: Meet Lhenvil Behind the Buzz
content:
# _We’re excited to share an exclusive interview with the creative mind whose artwork captivated_[ _  more than 400K viewers on CLO's Instagram_](https://www.instagram.com/p/C2fJcxPAALD/) _.    
Discover Lhenvil's story and the inspiration behind his stunning pieces._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/0951db1e85934821aa8b58e37e8153ef/images/8e72049776df458fa90f2d0606262e71DENIMVERSE_Concept_1.png)

> **_Please introduce yourself to CLO users._**

I am Lhenvil Paneda, a Filipino 3D fashion designer. I started out as a costume and fashion designer, designing and producing physical fashion. Due to the pandemic, I had to close my shop and find other avenues to earn a living. By watching YouTube tutorials and reading blogs, I was able to develop skills in digital fashion and improve on my work as the years went by. As of the moment, I am working with brands in creating 3D prototypes for their products, making their production pipeline more efficient and sustainable.  
  


> **_Could you  please elaborate on how you learned CLO through YouTube tutorials and blog posts?_**

Although I had zero knowledge of 3D prior to CLO, my experience in physical fashion production made it easier for me to understand the digital sewing process. To learn about CLO, I first started looking for tutorials on YouTube. I looked for the most complex ones first to further grasp what CLO can do. I then looked for the beginner tutorials mostly on the CLO YouTube channel. To further improve my skill set, I also looked for tutorials integrating CLO to various third party software. It is also important to always practice what you learn consistently.

 

> **_Please share the story or inspiration behind the artwork._**

The idea over this piece is upcycling old and unused jeans, and making them into a contemporary piece. Diving into the idea of sustainability, this piece consists of different pattern pieces salvaged from different pairs of pants. Denim fabric had this interesting structure so I made sure to highlight it by utilizing it on the pants overskirt and the sleeves.

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/0951db1e85934821aa8b58e37e8153ef/images/0524d4573be648b18ec367f6ea488d41DENIMVERSE_detail_2.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/0951db1e85934821aa8b58e37e8153ef/images/2ab9c9837af64e5aa1c5801b4da4324bMergedImages.png)

> **_Describe how and when you used CLO during the creation of this artwork._**

CLO was used in digitally creating this piece. With CLO's advanced features, I was able to draft patterns and sew the outfit on a digital avatar. Simulating and seeing how the patterns would drape in real life were also made easy. The outfit was also textured in CLO. The graphics tool was used in adding the denim wash while the puckering tool was used for the worn out and washed effect on the seams.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/0951db1e85934821aa8b58e37e8153ef/images/82b5bbca09b147e2820a3ff1a2aad5beScreenshot%202024-09-10%20122351.png)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/0951db1e85934821aa8b58e37e8153ef/images/51eccc186cf24722bef5ab166b844083Screenshot%202024-09-10%20122208.png)

> **_What was your favorite part of creating this piece?_**

My favorite part in creating this piece was the texturing part. It wasn't an easy task because getting the right settings for a realistic denim look was tricky, especially the wash and worn out parts. But trial and error is where the fun in creating is.

 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/0951db1e85934821aa8b58e37e8153ef/images/8da7b5d1ce664a39aa5bd383bc096080Screenshot%202024-09-10%20122232.png)

> **_What are your upcoming plans?_**

As of now, the plan is to improve my skill set to be able to offer more to my audience and to my clients. I believe that as technology progresses, so should one's skills.

 

> **_What advice would you give to users who are just beginning to use CLO?_**

My advice to users who are just beginning in CLO is to never get tired of learning something new. It may be a long and difficult process to reach the level you want to be, but everybody started at zero. I had no educational background in 3D but I was able to create with CLO with my willingness to learn.

* * *

_* If you want to learn how to create awesome denim textures like Lhenvil, check out this_[ _realistic denim jeans tutorial_](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u5fRb53raEU) _on our CLO YouTube channel._
content_description: Explore the inspiring journey of Lhenvil Paneda, a Filipino 3D fashion designer, as he shares his creative process and the sustainable vision behind his captivating artwork that has garnered over 400K views on CLO's Instagram.

title: Balenciaga X-Pander Spring Shoe
content:
## _Explore the Balenciaga X-Pander Spring Shoe, a game-ready 3D fashion creation designed with Marvelous Designer, blending precision and futuristic aesthetics._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/ce2621cd4e774107855c688bf69549a31-1.jpg)

# **Interview with  **[**Wallet**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/xDla8E)**  | Balenciaga X-Pander Spring Shoe****  | ****3D Artist**

* * *

# **Artist Introduction**

Hello everyone, I'm Wallet (我是你的小钱包呀！). I am a former senior 3D character artist at Activision Blizzard, having participated in projects like Destiny 2, Call of Duty 17, and Call of Duty 18, with 11 years of experience in realistic game development. I specialize in creating realistic character models and excel in modeling characters, hard surfaces, and clothing, particularly in detailing. Currently, I work at Tencent TiMi Studio, focusing on the creation of trendy clothing.

# **Tell us about the project - Balenciaga X-Pander Spring Shoe**

**Production Opportunity  **

The Balenciaga X-Pander spring shoes were a game model created in collaboration with the official Balenciaga brand for our company's game project. I needed to achieve scanning-level precision for this model and completed the high-accuracy production in Marvelous Designer.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/57fa951b00054573b36c2c9c3e0d6a311-3.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/8922364f21d04709bd203973de50604d1-2.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/f0287b1cf47f42b0a73c754828dd704a1-4.png)

**Material Collection  **

In the process of creating realistic models, I typically started by gathering a large amount of relevant materials, such as details from various aspects of the shoes, showcases of the shoe's shape, and resources that clearly displayed the structural details. Good reference materials significantly enhanced my production efficiency.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/9f2d8363ad0546239201b52ad5dc2f3a2-1.png)

**Creation of Sole and Last  **

The approach to making shoes differed slightly from that of regular clothing. For typical clothing, I could start directly in Marvelous Designer, but for shoes, I first created the last and sole. The sole served to stabilize the base, while the last shaped the overall structure of the shoe. In ZBrush, I sculpted a simple last based on reference images.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/c79262cff43543b9a8ce7d64cda533012-2.png)

Next, I created the sole based on this last. The sole of this shoe was quite complex, so I used Plasticity for its creation. This software was the most convenient and suitable NURBS modeling tool for game modeling that I had used in recent years. Especially with the introduction of new CV modeling, it had become even easier to work with. I used an older version without CV modeling, relying on traditional curves and boolean operations for the modeling process. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/79cc6e2412c8470ba3da8538f80ba2ae4.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/6591d484c3b74f068beb87e2091982783.png)

After completing the sole, I extracted the surfaces from it to use as the base pattern for the subsequent Marvelous Designer work. This pattern played a stabilizing role in Marvelous Designer.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/c9ef3fcd691a46ed94c922f0c2dab2685.png)

Since the pattern obtained from Plasticity did not have UVs, I also unwrapped the UVs in a 3D software.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/28d92fb589784e1c9b1f49f19bd01f676.png)

After obtaining the UVs, I imported them into Marvelous Designer by converting them for clothing use.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/94230099b50f4db284b15d6db10b11a57.png)

By selecting the 2D pattern on the UV map, I converted the model into a pattern piece.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/24f22b80c76f44d7b815260069a909a68.png)

Next, I will create the upper of the shoe based on this sole.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/1544cfcc05e24eea9b05fba41cdbec0f9.png)

**Marvelous Designer Pattern Making**

**Creating the Shoe Upper****  **

Using the previously created sole pattern, I began to extend and create the entire shoe pattern. The mesh upper was the most important part, and I chose to sculpt this model in ZBrush. I sculpted a rough shoe based on references and then retopologized it. Following the same method used for the sole, I created the upper, ensuring proper UV mapping. After converting it for clothing use and importing it into Marvelous Designer, I obtained the initial shoe upper pattern. The initially imported pattern had many unnecessary points, which I cleaned up.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/f7f29ca3d4294efa82469150c4ca859510.png)

**Creating the Upper Assembly Pattern Pieces****  **

For the other pattern pieces on the shoe upper, I prefer to use draping techniques. In Marvelous Designer, I can create these draped patterns using line segments.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/54fcabc9493b442d8b27c0bb44ed5b5311.png)

This approach allowed me to quickly draw pattern pieces directly onto the shoe upper.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/90bf93e8fb634a5bb62244b9f7cdb68912.png)

I selected the editing line segments and right-clicked to convert them into internal shapes.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/f615fc05a16643b58b2c599b318a533413.png)

By following this method, I was able to create all the pattern pieces. After obtaining these internal shapes, I pressed the "I" key to outline them as pattern pieces, completing the assembly pieces on the shoe upper.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/6cf8ba6d9d084a9787e1ea839e673d2414.png)

There were many assembly pattern pieces on the shoe upper, so in the end, I obtained a complex internal shape. I retained these internal shapes, as they would serve as the sewing edges for the subsequent sewing patterns.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/dfe1e56451ca4fddbf5c86c69128ba8615.png)

**Sewing Patterns****  **

For the majority of shoes, we typically assume that the pattern pieces are completely symmetrical, which makes the process much easier. Therefore, I only needed to create the pattern pieces for one side, and during sewing, I also only had to sew one side.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/ff42fa54e0d74b14b44a805cae07985416.png)

There wasn't much to say about the sewing patterns. The only aspect that needed emphasis was the overlapping relationships between the pattern pieces. While this wasn't complex, the process could be a bit tedious to operate.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/f96e3650e7974032aeda172639237e4617.png)

There were many instances of such layered sewing in this shoe. While following the realistic method of layering and sewing each piece was a bit cumbersome, it allowed for a more delicate representation of authenticity.

Realistic modeling focuses on ensuring that the overall shape is correct and visually appealing while paying attention to the creation of minute details. Only by doing so can a true sense of texture be achieved in the final presentation.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/95f47761ac58468d8e4765ea4656bdea18.png)

**Creating the Shoelaces****  **

The shoelaces for this shoe are round, so I couldn't simply use a single pattern piece. Instead, I used a double-layered sewing technique, which resulted in a much more natural appearance.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/97933f470d344c6da154b3821ed9d1ef19.png)

I created a faux effect for the shoelaces passing through the holes. Of course, it was possible to follow the realistic method of threading them through, but that was a bit more complicated. Instead, I directly sewed the shoelaces to the edges of the holes.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/df452890e37f4303a7da4e7907e6d18820.png)

**Final Adjustments****  **

In this step, I made overall minor adjustments to areas that differed from the references, correcting any interlacing or distortion issues caused by the complex sewing.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/64866689c69248ef88764b26ddf16b8b9c90483f73bf4fa0af9dc6a9af07cb0f.jpg)

Final Presentation on Marvelous Designer

**Creating the Mesh Texture in Substance 3D Designer****  **

The mesh for this shoe was quite unique, and after searching through existing mesh textures, I found that none were suitable. Therefore, I decided to create the mesh texture using Substance 3D Designer. Compared to the complex patterns typically made in Substance 3D Designer, creating this mesh was relatively simple. I later obtained a displacement map, which I used in ZBrush to convert into a model.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/1e1ab73dea0e4a4aaa0cbe27020adbd024.jpg)

**Refinement in ZBrush**

The process in ZBrush was similar to my usual clothing handling. I first cleaned up the mesh, using the workflow diagram from my previous racing suit project as a reference.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/a1aa6ab5a4ef4c70b898a0053b8d237125.png)

After cleaning up the mesh, I proceeded with the normal refinement work, which included:

  1. Adding wrinkle variations that Marvelous Designer couldn't handle

  2. Enhancing fabric changes at the seams

  3. Introducing memory folds

  4. Refining the edges

  5. Adding texture details

  6. Creating simple textures in ZBrush


![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/eb0c055b45b247c399055a5e818afd6026.png)

In ZBrush, I preferred to express all details through the model. For the shoe's detail creation, I divided the process into three layers:

  1. **Base Texture** : I selected base textures according to different materials.

  2. **Wear Effects** : Materials like leather and cotton are the most susceptible to showing wear. Leather develops cracks and wrinkles over time, while cotton forms memory folds.

  3. **Edge Details** : The front, back, and side of the leather exhibit three distinctly different textural states. The front is smooth due to processing and features the unique grain of the leather, while the side shows a cross-section, revealing the torn appearance of the leather. For the shoelaces, the front is woven, and the side shows the seams of the weaving. Addressing these details significantly enhances the overall realism.




**Final Rendering**

For the final rendering, I used Keyshot, primarily because it supports a very high polygon count. Renderers like Blender and Marmoset cannot handle high-resolution models, and I prefer not to create low-poly versions. Therefore, Keyshot was an excellent choice, and I also opted to create the materials directly within Keyshot.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/6e1ab00454e742fab78792c619bec679/images/d714340faaec4448aeff52370348ba7a32.png)

**Summary**

The shoe creation process was quite intricate, especially in achieving the special interlacing design within the streamlined structure, which took considerable time while also ensuring the stability of the shoe shape. Additionally, the detail handling in ZBrush was time-consuming. In terms of Marvelous Designer, the requirements for pattern-making in shoe design were relatively lower, making the process simpler compared to clothing creation.

# **In your "Balenciaga X-Pander Spring Shoe" project, you used Marvelous Designer for the initial pattern making. What made you choose Marvelous Designer for this process?**

The draping feature in Marvelous Designer is extremely convenient, allowing me to easily create the intricate pattern pieces on the shoe upper. Most importantly, it supports modifications at any time. While traditional methods can also quickly produce models, they are relatively cumbersome to modify, especially when dealing with complex patterns. Additionally, although the shoe's materials are stiff and less prone to wrinkles, the shoes made in Marvelous Designer may lack some realism. However, they still exhibit a certain degree of authenticity. The fabric simulation in Marvelous Designer can convey subtle realism, making it more natural than hand-sculpting.

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

The entire process involved using Marvelous Designer for initial pattern-making, Substance 3D Designer for creating the shoe's mesh, Plasticity for the sole construction, ZBrush for detailing, and Keyshot for the final rendering.

# **Are there any areas/ideas you would like to utilize Marvelous Designer in your future project?**

Yes, I will continue to use Marvelous Designer in other game projects, as well as in my own design projects. I am currently working on a new tutorial case.

# **Are there any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer that you can share with the community?**

Marvelous Designer is essentially a garment design software, so to create reasonable and aesthetically pleasing clothing, users need to possess certain pattern-making skills and basic knowledge of garment construction. This will better assist them in achieving their desired design outcomes.

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

Among the various fabric simulation software and plugins I use, Marvelous Designer is irreplaceable. Although it may be slightly inconvenient compared to some emerging software or plugins in certain aspects, this does not detract from its outstanding and precise simulation results.

# **by  ****Wallet (我是你的小钱包呀！)**  
[**_Artstation_**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/xDla8E)
content_description: Discover the innovative Balenciaga X-Pander Spring Shoe, a cutting-edge 3D fashion design that merges high precision with futuristic style, crafted using Marvelous Designer.
